articles.title: Ancient school where Aristotle taught Alexander the Great has been unearthed by archaeologists in Greece
articles.description: In an extraordinary archaeological discovery in northern Greece, a gymnasium complex tied to Alexander the Great's education has emerged in Mieza. Believed to have been established by King Philip II, this site functioned as a prestigious institution for the elite. Recent excavations revealed various structures, including banquet halls used for social gatherings and teaching facilities, hinting at Aristotle's influence on students like Alexander.

articles.title: Private Effort Protects Reservoir: Landowner’s project restores creek; safeguards Kinkaid Lake water
articles.description: Greg Reising began his conservation work on his 100-acre property near Kinkaid Lake in 1995. He transformed former agricultural land by establishing prairie vegetation and planting thousands of trees. Erosion and sedimentation problems in the Kinkaid Lake watershed led to broader conservation efforts involving various agencies. The Environmental Quality Incentives Program supported Reising's initiatives, including streambank stabilization and habitat improvement measures.

articles.title: Stock market today: Sensex tumbles over 600 points, Nifty50 below 22,650
articles.full_text: In Asian markets, South Korea’s KOSPI, Japan's Nikkei 225 index and Hong Kong's Hang Seng index traded lower, while Shanghai's SSE Composite index quoted marginally higher. Stock Market today: Why is the market crashing? Oil prices remain a key factor weighing on Indian benchmark indices. Crude prices rose for a second consecutive session on Tuesday as concerns over potential disruptions to Middle East supplies due to the US-Iran conflict outweighed signs of recovering crude exports from the region. Disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz have also continued for the seventh consecutive month, while a stalemate in US-Iran peace talks has added to supply concerns. Earlier, US President Donald Trump rejected an Iranian proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and end the conflict. Analysts said the surge in crude prices following the US-Iran stalemate, along with continued foreign fund outflows, a spike in US bond yields and weak Asian markets, triggered broad-based selling. Foreign Institutional Investors (FIIs) offloaded equities worth Rs 3,693.93 crore on Friday, according to exchange data, adding to the pressure on domestic markets. The rupee depreciated 16 paise and slumped below the psychologically important 96 per dollar level in early trade on Tuesday weighed down by elevated crude oil prices and persistent foreign fund outflows. Forex traders said the rupee is under pressure largely due to the combination of firm oil and rising US nominal and real yields, which together are drawing portfolio flows out of emerging markets, including India. At the interbank foreign exchange market, the rupee opened at 96.03, then fell to 96.13 against the US dollar, registering a fall of 16 paise from its previous close. On Monday, the rupee had settled at 95.97 against the American currency. Oil prices today: Brent Crude rises for second session as US-Iran conflict fuels supply concerns Gold steadied on Tuesday but remained near a more than seven-week low as concerns that the US Federal Reserve could keep interest rates higher for longer weighed on the precious metal. Investors also awaited a series of US economic data for clues on the interest-rate outlook. Spot gold was little changed at $4,124.57 per ounce as of 0140 GMT, after touching its lowest level since August 5 in the previous session. US gold futures fell 0.3% to $4,156.70. Stock market crash today: BSE Sensex crashes over 1,100 points, investors lose Rs 8.92 lakh crore - top reasons for fall BSE Sensex and Nifty50, the Indian equity benchmarks tanked in morning trade on Monday as persistently high crude oil prices and a spike in US bond yields added to investors’ woes. Both indices crashed over 1% amid the intensifying Iran-US conflict. While Sensex crashed over 1,100 points, Nifty50 went below 22,800. BSE Sensex ended the day at 72,771.72, down 1,124 points or 1.52%. Nifty50 closed at 22,780.25, down 360 points or 1.56%.The selloff also erased nearly Rs 8.92 lakh crore from the combined market capitalisation of BSE-listed companies, taking it down to around Rs 474 lakh crore.

articles.title: Five Indiana engineering students built a 12-hour wearable that helps visually impaired users detect obstacles beyond a cane or guide dog
articles.description: Rose-Hulman students have developed a remarkable wearable device tailored for visually impaired individuals. This innovative headgear employs advanced sensors to identify surrounding obstacles, providing users with haptic feedback. With a remarkable twelve-hour battery life on a single charge, this device empowers users with greater independence. The project's goal is to enhance the day-to-day experiences of those with vision impairments.
